In this petition, the petitioner is seeking bail in crime No.13/2002 numbered in C.C.No.52/2003 on the file of Civil Judge and J.M.F.C., Bagepalli for the offence punishable under Section 419 and 420 of I.P.C.
2.
Heard Sri. Gangadhar. K, learned counsel for the petitioner and learned HCGP for respondent-State.
3. It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioner that after the incident, the petitioner was assisted for the investigation, he was arrested and released on bail.

After release on bail, the petitioner fell ill, he was under depression, taking treatment, he was not aware of the filing of the chargesheet and he has not received any summons to appear before the Court to face the trial.
Under such circumstances, he was declared as proclaimed offender.
When he returned to the village

,
he was arrested and subjected to judicial custody.
He is ready to face the trial and imposing any conditions, he may be granted bail.

4. Per contra, learned HCGP has submitted that the alleged incident took place in the year 2002 and the NC: 2023:KHC:37751 chargesheet was filed in the year 2003, even 20 years thereafter, the petitioner was not secured for trial.
If bail is granted, he will again abscond and cause hindrance to the trial.
5. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the material on record.
6. The material on record did point out that the petitioner was granted bail on personal bond and surety before the Trial Court.
On the ground of illness, the petitioner did not appear for the trial and he shifted to Tamil Nadu.
For this reason he was declared as proclaimed offender.
The allegation against the petitioner is that he has used someone's marks card to gain the employment for the post of teacher.
When it was unearthed, he was dismissed from the service and now he has to face trial before the Court.
The matter is ready for trial.
The presence of the petitioner is secured.
There is no dispute that he is a permanent resident of Yadahalli Village, Mulubagilu Taluk.
Having regard to the gravity of the offence, it is not proper to keep the petitioner in judicial custody as a pre-trial condition.
Conditions will meet the apprehension of the NC: 2023:KHC:37751 prosecution.

In the result, the following:-

ii) Petitioner is to ordered to be released on self-bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties for like sum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.
iii) The petitioner shall regularly appear before Trial Court to face the trial.

iv) Since the petitioner has breached the conditions of bond executed earlier, he has to clear the bond amount before the Trial Court first and it shall be appropriated to Government.
